description: Waterfall Effects on Native and Non-Native Fish Movement in the San Juan River is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. The accumulation of sediment when the reservoir was full and the subsequent decline in water levels resulted in the river rerouting out of the original channel to a sandstone ledge and forming a waterfall at Piute Farms, upstream of the San Juan River inflow to Lake Powell. Coverage: San Juan River (2022). The toolkit gives San Juan River as the location, 2022 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
